title: I’m making a sci-fi game with AI tools. Here’s what I’ve learned so far
author: Exciting-Pool5495
selftext:
Hey everyone! I’m Adam, and I’m making a game called **Krakatoa Circle 2**.

It’s a third-person action game set on a moon, with fast movement and bullet-hell combat inspired by games I love like *Returnal* and *Saros*. The main character, Asha, is sent to guard a dig site. Things get a little weird when she finds a huge alien door leading deeper into the moon.

The story is still early, but I’ve been thinking about a question: is all knowledge good? What happens when we find something we maybe shouldn’t have gone looking for?

I’m also playing with the idea that upgrades could change Asha’s personality, not just her abilities. Maybe an upgrade that makes her faster also makes her more impatient. Or one that lets her see through walls makes it harder for her to look inward. I’m still figuring it out, but I think it could be fun to have the story change along with the way you play.

Here’s some of the concept art I’ve been using to find the look of the world:



**How I’m making it**

I like starting with Midjourney because I find its images the most interesting to look at. I’ll take an image I like, use ChatGPT to change or develop it, and then crop out an object I want to bring into the game. I make that crop clearer and bigger, then use Tripo to turn it into a 3D model.

Here’s an example using an excavator:



The model still needs work after that. It might be the wrong size, look strange from another angle, get in the player’s way, or slow the game down. So I bring it into the game, look at it, try it out, and keep tweaking.

If you’re curious about trying Tripo, these guides are useful:

* [Turning an image into a 3D model](https://www.tripo3d.ai/help/features/how-to-use-the-image-to-3d-feature)
* [Getting a cleaner reference image](https://www.tripo3d.ai/blog/25-image-to-3d-prompt-tips-for-cleaner-ai-3d-models)
* [Getting your model out of Tripo and into a game](https://www.tripo3d.ai/product-doc/export-and-integration/export-dcc)

  


**Something funny i tried that that didn’t work**

I tried setting up Claude like a tiny game studio, with a director, managers, workers, scorecards and hourly OKRs. The idea was that the managers would keep everyone organized and moving in the right direction.

It got out of hand. I had around 22 sessions going, but the level wasn’t getting any better. Too much time went into coordinating, big batches of changes weren’t getting checked soon enough, and my computer could only handle so much at once. I ended up dropping the manager setup and going back to a smaller group focused on making and testing things.



The big lesson for me was that I can’t play a status report. I need to see what’s changed and actually try the game.

I’ve wanted to make games for a long time, and AI has helped me start making something I didn’t think I could build from scratch. It’s still early, and there’s a lot to figure out, but I’m having a lot of fun with it.

I’d love to hear what you think. Does the setting or the idea of upgrades changing Asha’s personality sound interesting? And if you’ve tried using AI for a creative project, what worked for you and what turned into a headache?
